subject: English Home Language

source.subtopic: Shared: reads fiction and non-fiction; answers higher-order questions ('In your opinion...'); says whether a story was liked and justifies it; recognises apostrophes in contractions and possession (John's car, don't)

show.line: The little flying comma is an apostrophe. Do not becomes don't. John's car means the car belongs to John.

rounds.prompt: Which card shows the short way to write do not?
Read this short word. It means can not.
Whose ball is it? Read the card. Sipho's ball.
rounds.praise: Yes! The apostrophe shows it belongs to Sipho.

rounds.prompt: Which card has the apostrophe in the right place for the dog's bone?
rounds.praise: Yes! The bone belongs to the dog.

rounds.prompt: Read this. It is short for it is.
Short for two words, or shows who owns it? Put each card in its group.
In your opinion, is Sipho's ball a good present? Tap what you think.
rounds.praise: Thank you for sharing your opinion!

hints: The apostrophe takes the place of missing letters. Do not, don't.
Name, apostrophe, then s means it belongs to that person.

beat_the_tutor.setup: My turn! I will read this card. Gogo's hat.
beat_the_tutor.tutor_try: This says Gogo is a hat!
beat_the_tutor.win_line: You caught me! The apostrophe means the hat belongs to Gogo.
beat_the_tutor.gentle_line: Let's read it together. Gogo's hat. The hat belongs to Gogo!

parent_line: Can recognise an apostrophe in short forms like don't and in Sipho's ball.
